title: Consciousness can exist without a self or first-person perspective

statements.text: Perspectivalness is not a necessary condition of consciousness. In some spiritual and religious experiences and in fully depersonalized psychiatric states, the most plausible reading of the phenomenology is that no conscious self and no experienced first-person perspective exist. These are states of non-subjective consciousness.

sources.quote: perspectivalness is not a necessary condition for the ascription of conscious experience to a given system
I take such global experiential states to be instances of non-subjective consciousness.
